cases.sentence: У окна ___ с приходо-расходными книгами и бумагами всякого рода, конторка, шкапы, весы.
cases.explain: «большой стол» — the accusative marks the direct object of the verb.
cases.translation: VOITSKI'S bedroom, which is also his office. A table stands near the window; on it are ledgers, letter scales, and papers of every description. Near by stands a smaller table belonging to ASTROFF, with his paints and drawing materials. On the wall hangs a cage containing a starling. There is also a map of Africa on the wall, obviously of no use to anybody. There is a large sofa covered with buckram. A door to the left leads into an inner room; one to the right leads into the front hall, and before this door lies a mat for the peasants with their muddy boots to stand on. It is an autumn evening. The silence is profound. TELEGIN and MARINA are sitting facing one another, winding wool.

cases.sentence: С ___, мне давно уже нужно уехать отсюда, но, повторяю, я не уеду, пока ты не возвратишь того, что взял у меня.
cases.explain: «большим удовольствием» — after the preposition «с», the instrumental marks the means, company, or complement.
cases.translation: ASTROFF. I would, with the greatest pleasure. I ought to have gone long ago, but I shan't leave you until you have returned what you took from me.

cases.sentence: (___.) Я — сумасшедший, а не сумасшедшие те, которые под личиной профессора, ученого мага, прячут свою бездарность, тупость, свое вопиющее бессердечие.
cases.explain: «Злой смех» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: VOITSKI. [Shrugging his shoulders] Strange! I attempted murder, and am not going to be arrested or brought to trial. That means they think me mad. [With a bitter laugh] Me! I am mad, and those who hide their worthlessness, their dullness, their crying heartlessness behind a professor's mask, are sane! Those who marry old men and then deceive them under the noses of all, are sane! I saw you kiss her; I saw you in each other's arms!

cases.explain: «сумасшедшая земля» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: VOITSKI. [His eyes on the door] No, it is the earth that is mad, because she still bears us on her breast.

cases.sentence: Прежде и я всякого чудака считал больным, ненормальным, а теперь я такого мнения, что ___ человека — это быть чудаком.
cases.explain: «нормальное состояние» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: ASTROFF. This is a farce! You are not mad; you are simply a ridiculous fool. I used to think every fool was out of his senses, but now I see that lack of sense is a man's normal state, and you are perfectly normal.

cases.sentence: Это ___ стыда не может сравниться ни с какою болью.
cases.explain: «острое чувство» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: VOITSKI. [Covers his face with his hands] Oh! If you knew how ashamed I am! These piercing pangs of shame are like nothing on earth. [In an agonised voice] I can't endure them! [He leans against the table] What can I do? What can I do?

cases.sentence: Но в какие-нибудь десять лет жизнь обывательская, жизнь презренная затянула нас; она своими ___ отравила нашу кровь, и мы стали такими же пошляками, как все.
cases.explain: «гнилыми испарениями» — the instrumental marks the means, company, or complement.
cases.translation: ASTROFF. [Shouts angrily] Stop! [Then, more gently] It may be that posterity, which will despise us for our blind and stupid lives, will find some road to happiness; but we--you and I--have but one hope, the hope that we may be visited by visions, perhaps by pleasant ones, as we lie resting in our graves. [Sighing] Yes, brother, there were only two respectable, intelligent men in this county, you and I. Ten years or so of this life of ours, this miserable life, have sucked us under, and we have become as contemptible and petty as the rest. But don't try to talk me out of my purpose! Give me what you took from me, will you?

cases.sentence: Ты взял у меня из ___ баночку с морфием.
cases.explain: «дорожной аптеки» — after the preposition «из», the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: ASTROFF. You took a little bottle of morphine out of my medicine-case. [A pause] Listen! If you are positively determined to make an end to yourself, go into the woods and shoot yourself there. Give up the morphine, or there will be a lot of talk and guesswork; people will think I gave it to you. I don't fancy having to perform a post-mortem on you. Do you think I should find it interesting?

cases.sentence: Я увлекся, ___ ничего не делал, а в это время люди болели, в лесах моих, лесных порослях, мужики пасли свой скот…
cases.explain: «целый месяц» — the accusative marks the direct object of the verb.
cases.translation: ASTROFF. [Pressing her hand] Yes, go. [Thoughtfully] You seem to be sincere and good, and yet there is something strangely disquieting about all your personality. No sooner did you arrive here with your husband than every one whom you found busy and actively creating something was forced to drop his work and give himself up for the whole summer to your husband's gout and yourself. You and he have infected us with your idleness. I have been swept off my feet; I have not put my hand to a thing for weeks, during which sickness has been running its course unchecked among the people, and the peasants have been pasturing their cattle in my woods and young plantations. Go where you will, you and your husband will always carry destruction in your train. I am joking of course, and yet I am strangely sure that had you stayed here we should have been overtaken by the most immense desolation. I would have gone to my ruin, and you--you would not have prospered. So go! E finita la comedia!

cases.sentence: После того, что случилось, в эти несколько часов я так много пережил и столько передумал, что, кажется, мог бы написать в назидание потомству ___ о том, как надо жить.
cases.explain: «целый трактат» — the accusative marks the direct object of the verb.
cases.translation: SEREBRAKOFF. [To VOITSKI] Shame on him who bears malice for the past. I have gone through so much in the last few hours that I feel capable of writing a whole treatise on the conduct of life for the instruction of posterity. I gladly accept your apology, and myself ask your forgiveness. [He kisses VOITSKI three times.]

cases.sentence: Я уважаю ваш образ мыслей, ваши увлечения, порывы, но позвольте старику внести в мой ___ только одно замечание: надо, господа, дело делать!
cases.explain: «прощальный привет» — after the preposition «в», the accusative marks the direct object of the verb.
cases.translation: SEREBRAKOFF. [Kissing his daughter] Good-bye, good-bye all. [Shaking hands with ASTROFF] Many thanks for your pleasant company. I have a deep regard for your opinions and your enthusiasm, but let me, as an old man, give one word of advice at parting: do something, my friend! Work! Do something! [They all bow] Good luck to you all. [He goes out followed by MME. VOITSKAYA and SONIA.]

cases.explain: «старого долга» — the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: VOITSKI. [Writing] And carry forward from the old debt two seventy-five--

cases.sentence: (Подходит к карте Африки и смотрит на нее.) А, должно быть, в этой самой Африке теперь жарища — ___!
cases.explain: «страшное дело» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: ASTROFF. I shall have to go around by the blacksmith's on my way home. It can't be avoided. [He stands looking up at the map of Africa hanging on the wall] I suppose it is roasting hot in Africa now.
